story.value: Thorium is named after Thor, the Scandinavian god of thunder.
Thorium was discovered in 1828 by the Swedish chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius.
Thorium was first isolated in 1914 by the chemists D. Lely, Jr. and L. Hamburger.

uses.value: In the past, thorium's main use was making Welsbach mantles for portable gaslights.
Thorium oxide is used to make glass for high quality camera lenses.
Thorium is used to coat tungsten filaments in electronic devices, such as television sets.
Thorium is used as an alloying agent to make magnesium stronger at high temperatures.
